sections.h2: What is Broomfield, and who handles its property tax?
sections.html:
Broomfield is a consolidated city and county between Denver and Boulder along US 36 and US 287. Because it is both, the City and County of Broomfield runs its own Assessor, Treasurer and Clerk and Recorder under one roof at One DesCombes Drive.

That makes Broomfield different from most Colorado places, where a county office bills for the cities inside it. Here a single government assesses the value, sends the bill and records the deed.

The Treasurer's number is 303-464-5810, and the Assessor is at 303-464-5819 or assessor@broomfield.org.

sections.h2: How did Broomfield become a city and county?
sections.html:
Broomfield was incorporated as a city on June 6, 1961, in the southeast corner of Boulder County, and became a consolidated city and county on November 15, 2001. A 1998 constitutional amendment made the new county possible.

By the 1990s the city had annexed land in Adams, Jefferson and Weld counties as well, so it was built from four counties. The name comes from broomcorn, a sorghum grown in the area, and the post office opened on September 26, 1884. The Denver-Boulder Turnpike opened January 19, 1952 and became free on September 14, 1967.

For sellers, the 2001 date matters. Broomfield's online recording portal covers documents recorded from November 2001, and older records may sit with Adams, Boulder, Jefferson or Weld.

sections.html:
Roughly 63% of Broomfield homes are owner-occupied. These are the Census Bureau's QuickFacts figures for the county, which is the same boundary as the city.

sections.h2: Who are the major employers in Broomfield?
sections.html:
Oracle America leads the list with 1,650 employees, according to a 2023 employer list. The five largest are shown below.

  • Oracle America: 1,650
  • Intermountain Health Care: 1,550
  • BAE Systems: 1,100
  • Hunter Douglas Window Fashions Division: 950
  • City and County of Broomfield: 900

Crocs, Vail Resorts and Webroot also have headquarters in the city.

sections.h2: What is Broomfield's climate, and how does it affect a house?
sections.html:
Broomfield has a cold semi-arid climate, with about 16 inches of precipitation a year. It sits in USDA hardiness zone 6a.

The mean daily high is 88.7 degrees in July and 45.4 in January, and the mean low is 57.6 in July and 18.3 in January. A house here goes through large swings between hot summers and cold winter nights.

Those swings are hard on roofs, exterior paint and heating systems. The 2021 Marshall Fire put parts of Broomfield under pre-evacuation orders, though the fire's destruction was in Superior, Louisville and unincorporated Boulder County.

sections.h2: What schools and roads serve Broomfield?
sections.html:
Six school districts reach into Broomfield, and the city was assembled from parts of four counties. They are listed below.

  • Boulder Valley School District
  • 27J Schools
  • Weld County School District RE-8
  • Jefferson County Public Schools
  • St. Vrain Valley School District
  • Adams 12 Five Star Schools

Your address decides which district's mill levy applies, so two houses a mile apart can see different bills. US 36 and US 287 run through the city, and Rocky Mountain Metropolitan Airport is nearby.

sections.h2: When is Broomfield property tax due?
sections.html:
Broomfield's Treasurer lists February 28 for the first half, June 15 for the second half, and April 30 for a full payment. No interest accrues if you pay by those dates.

Tax notices go to the owner of record, not the mortgage company, around the third week of January, by email or mail. If your lender pays from escrow, check with them. Taxes under $25 must use the full-tax option.

Payment optionDueLate interest starts
First halfFebruary 281% in March, rising to 10% in December
Second halfJune 151% in late June, rising to 7% in December
Full paymentApril 301% in May, rising to 8% in December

After a due date, call 303-438-6390 for updated figures.

sections.h2: How can you pay Broomfield property tax?
sections.html:
You can pay in cash, by check, by eCheck or by credit card. The credit card provider charges 2.50%, and an eCheck costs $2.50. Online payments are capped at $1,000,000 per transaction.

The office is in the George Di Ciero City and County Building at One DesCombes Drive. The Treasurer's page also mentions a senior tax deferral program, with the application at colorado.propertytaxdeferral.com. A Certificate of Taxes Due, governed by C.R.S. 39-10-115, confirms that all taxes are paid except those listed as still due.

Broomfield reappraises in odd-numbered years and carries values forward in even years unless something changes. The assessment date is January 1 each year.

For the 2025 and 2026 reappraisals, residential sales from July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2024 are used. Only qualified arms-length sales count. The Assessor uses the market approach for homes, and its appraisers are licensed by Colorado and follow USPAP guidelines.

In an even year, a notice goes out only if something changed, such as a finished basement, an addition or a demolition. The page says tax is assessment rate times value times tax rate, and that the state legislature sets the rate while taxing authorities set the mill levy.

sections.h2: How do you protest a Broomfield valuation?
sections.html:
File with the Assessor between May 1 and June 8 for real property. Personal property protests are due by June 30.

  • Online: the appeal portal at appeals.spatialest.com/co-broomfield, which includes a neighborhood sales map and document uploads.
  • Mail: the Real Property Protest Form, postmarked by June 8, to PO Box 1149, Broomfield, CO 80038-1149.
  • In person: the Community Assistance Center in the main lobby of the City and County Building.

Useful evidence includes an appraisal dated 7/1/2022 to 6/30/2024, photos of condition, comparable sales and proof of record errors. A Notice of Determination is sent by June 30 for real property.

If you disagree, you can go to the Board of Equalization, whose deadlines are July 15 for real property and July 20 for personal property. Hearings are held remotely, run by an independent hearing officer, and you carry the burden of showing your value is more accurate. Evidence files must be 20 MB or smaller. The board's contact is clk-boe@broomfield.org or 303-438-6332, option 9. The Assessor's valuation page lists hearings in late July and a finish by August 5.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed cost in Broomfield?
sections.html:
Broomfield's schedule effective June 1, 2026 sets a flat $43 for the first page of a recorded document, with no charge for added pages. The city's recording page describes it as a $40 fee plus a $3 surcharge per document.

The documentary fee is $0.01 per $100 of consideration over $500, so a $500,000 transfer pays $50. Treasurer's, public trustee's and sheriff's deeds are exempt. The Recording Division is open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and documents can be mailed, dropped off, brought in or e-recorded.

Documents need a one-inch top and bottom margin and half-inch side margins, a return address and a signed check payable to the City and County of Broomfield. The office cannot give legal advice on which document to file.

sections.h2: What happens when you sell a Broomfield house with tax due?
sections.html:
The title company pays any unpaid property tax from your proceeds at closing. Ask the Treasurer for current figures before you set a date, because interest grows monthly.

Broomfield's first half is due in February, a few days earlier than Boulder County's March 2. A seller who closes in late winter should confirm whether that first half has been paid.

faqs.q: When are Broomfield property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due February 28, the second half June 15, and a full payment April 30. Interest starts at 1% the month after a missed date.

faqs.q: Does Broomfield have a separate county government?
faqs.a: Yes. Broomfield became a consolidated city and county on November 15, 2001, so one government assesses, bills and records.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to protest a Broomfield valuation?
faqs.a: June 8 for real property. Appeals to the Board of Equalization follow, with a July 15 deadline for real property.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Broomfield?
faqs.a: The flat recording fee is $43 per document under the schedule effective June 1, 2026. Add the documentary fee of $0.01 per $100 over $500.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Broomfield house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Closing agents pay the balance from the sale proceeds. Call the Treasurer at 303-464-5810 or 303-438-6390 for the exact amount.
